title: What is Chatalyst
description: Chatalyst is one plugin for your server's chat, moderation and community tools. Start here to see what it does and whether it fits your server.
headings: What you get on day one
text: Chatalyst is a chat plugin for Minecraft servers. It makes every message look good, keeps chat clean and gives your staff the tools to look after the community. It replaces the usual pile of separate chat, filter and moderation plugins with one jar that is set up in minutes. You do not need to be technical to use it. A fresh install already gives you a styled chat, channels, mentions, private messages and a spam and swear filter. Everything else is optional and comes switched off, so your server only runs what you choose. # What you get on day one These are on as soon as you install Chatalyst: Feature What it does for you Chat formats Each message shows the player's rank, name and text in a clean style. Hovering a name shows rank, party, money, time played and ping. Channels Separate rooms for global, staff, local (radio), region and party chat. Mentions Writing a player's name highlights it and plays a sound for them. Private messages /msg , /reply and /ignore . Filter and anti-spam Blocks spam, flooding, caps abuse, swearing and hidden-character tricks. Rules Ready-made rules that stop advertising and server IPs. Chat log A daily log of chat so staff can check what happened. Warning points Infractions add points; too many points mute or kick automatically. # Optional extras Turn these on only if you want them. Turn on extras shows how, and /cht features lists them in game: Moderation: staff suite (bans, freeze, vanish), reports , anonymous mode , anti-bot, command blocker.

title: Turn on extras
description: Chatalyst ships with only the chat on. Use /cht features to see every optional feature and switch on the ones you want.
text: Chatalyst is a chat plugin first. A new install turns on the chat and its protections, and leaves every other feature off. That way your server only runs what you actually use, and nothing surprises your players. This page shows how to see what is on, and how to switch an extra on in two steps. # See what is on Run this in game or in the console: text Copy It prints two lists. On shows what is running. It needs chatalyst.admin . # Turn an extra on Open the file named in the list, inside plugins/Chatalyst/ . Find the setting and change false to true . title: License & activation
description: How your license works when you buy on BuiltByBit, what the check sends, what happens without internet, and how author-issued keys work.
text: Chatalyst is a paid plugin by DevKazuo. This page explains how the license works, what it sends and what happens if something fails, so there are no surprises. # Bought on BuiltByBit Your purchase is the license. title: Privacy
description: What Chatalyst sends outside your server, who receives it, how long it is kept and how to ask for it to be deleted.
text: This page covers the data that reaches the author or BuiltByBit because of your license. It does not cover what your own server stores about your players. That data stays on your server and you decide what to keep. See Spy & logs and Storage & database . # Who is responsible Chatalyst is made by DevKazuo. For any privacy question or request, open a ticket on the Kazuo Community Discord . # Bought on BuiltByBit Nothing is sent to the author. Your server contacts only BuiltByBit: License check: once at startup, with the resource id and your BuiltByBit member id. Update check: at startup, if Updates.Check is true . It asks BuiltByBit for the latest version, or your own address if you set Updates.Url . Set Updates.Check to false in config.yml to turn it off. BuiltByBit handles these requests under its own privacy policy. Chatalyst keeps the last signed answer on your server so it can start during a BuiltByBit outage. # Keys issued by the author If you use a key from the author, the plugin contacts the author's license service on startup, every 6 hours and once a day. This service runs on Cloudflare and posts notices to a private Discord channel. title: Updating
description: Update Chatalyst by swapping the jar. Your settings are kept and new options are added for you.
headings: If something looks wrong after an update
text: Updating Chatalyst is a jar swap. Your configuration, player data and the features you turned on are kept. New options that come with an update are added to your files automatically. # Update in three steps Stop the server. Replace the old Chatalyst-<version>.jar in plugins/ with the new one. Remove the old jar so only one Chatalyst jar is left. Start the server and check the console for the Chatalyst banner. Warning A new jar always needs a full restart. /cht reload only re-reads the YAML files; it cannot load new code. # What happens to your files Every file has an internal version ( Config_Version in config.yml ). On startup Chatalyst adds the options that are new in this version and keeps every value you changed. Do not edit or remove Config_Version . The on/off switches of the optional features are never changed. If you left mail off, it stays off after the update. Player data (nicknames, mail, mutes, warnings, titles) is kept as it is. # Get told about new versions Chatalyst can check for a newer version on startup and tell admins when they join. It never downloads anything by itself. The settings are in config.yml : yaml Copy Check turns the check on or off: set it to false to turn it off. With Url empty, BuiltByBit copies ask BuiltByBit for the latest version. Set Url only to use your own address instead. # If something looks wrong after an update Run /cht doctor . text: Quick answers to common questions. For problems with a clear symptom, see Common problems . # Does it work on Spigot? No. Chatalyst uses Paper features, so it needs Paper, Purpur or Folia. See Compatibility & conflicts . # Which Minecraft and Java versions? Minecraft 1.21.1 to 26.3. Use Java 21 for 1.21.1 to 1.21.11, and Java 25 for 26.1 and newer. # Do I need PlaceholderAPI or LuckPerms? No, both are optional. With LuckPerms, ranks and their colors appear in chat automatically. PlaceholderAPI adds %placeholders% from other plugins. The default format uses %luckperms_prefix% ; without PlaceholderAPI, swap it for {player_prefix} . # Can I keep my current chat plugin? Use only one plugin that formats chat, or they will fight over each message. Moderation and other plugins are fine. See Compatibility & conflicts . # Does it replace EssentialsX? Mail lives at /inbox so it never clashes with Essentials' /mail . # Why are so many features off? On purpose. A new install only turns on the chat and its protections, so your server runs only what you use. /cht features lists the extras and how to turn each one on. text: A chat format decides how a message looks: the rank prefix, the name, the separator and the message, each with its own hover text and click action. title: Channels
description: Separate chat rooms for global, trade, staff, radio, region and party chat, with history replay and a router that keeps sales out of global chat.
text: Channels split your chat into rooms. Every player writes in one channel at a time and reads the channels they are allowed to hear. A survival server can keep sales in trade , staff talk in staff and nearby conversations on a radio frequency, while global chat stays readable. Channels are on by default. The shipped layout has global , local (radio), staff , region and party ready to use, and trade and auction prepared but disabled. # Channel types Type Who receives the message GLOBAL Everyone on the server. With Proxy: true , the whole network. WORLD Players in the same world. FREQUENCY Players tuned to the same radio frequency, at any distance. REGION Players standing in the same chat region (Chatalyst regions or WorldGuard regions). PARTY Members of the same party (Parties plugin). Note REGION and PARTY channels behave like normal channels when WorldGuard or Parties is missing, so nothing breaks. # How to turn it on Everything lives in plugins/Chatalyst/chat.yml under Channels . The module is enabled out of the box: yaml Copy Run /cht reload after editing. # Configuration # Global options Option Default What it does Enabled true Master switch for the channel system. Default global The main chat. New players write here. On_Join default default puts everyone back in the default channel on join. last remembers the channel they left in. Exclusive true Channels act as separate rooms (see below). false goes back to overlapping channels. History.Enabled true Keeps a short in-memory

title: Mentions
description: Play a sound and highlight the name when someone is mentioned in chat, by real name or nickname, with a per-player off switch.
text: Mentions make sure people notice when they are talked to. When a message names a player, that player hears a sound and sees their own name highlighted in the line. Nobody else sees the highlight. A mention works with the real name and with the nickname, because the nickname is often the only name other players know. It also works with the alias of a player in anonymous mode . # How to turn it on Mentions are on by default. The settings live in plugins/Chatalyst/chat.yml : yaml Copy Run /cht reload after editing. # Configuration Option Default What it does Enabled true Turns mention sounds on or off. Cooldown_Seconds 0 Minimum seconds between two pings for the same player. 0 = no cooldown. Capped at one hour. Require_At false true = only @name counts. false = the bare name counts too. Sound minecraft:block.note_block.pling Namespaced sound key. Highlight.Enabled true Highlights the mentioned name in the line, only for the mentioned player. Highlight.Color yellow Highlight color. Highlight.Bold true Makes the highlighted name bold. # How a mention is detected The name must appear as a whole word. @Notch , Notch, and notch. all count. Notchy does not. Case does not matter. Only players who actually receive the message are pinged. A player in another channel or on another radio frequency is not. The sender never pings themselves. # Commands and permissions Command Permission What it does /toggle mentions chatalyst.command.toggle (true) Each player can turn the mention sound off f

title: Private messages
description: Instant /msg and /reply between online players, with ignore lists, a personal off switch, staff spy and an optional fallback to mail.
text: Private messages are instant, one-to-one conversations between players who are online on the same server. They come with a persistent ignore list, a personal switch to stop receiving them, their own formats and optional visibility for staff through spy. Private messages are part of chat and ship enabled . Mail , which also reaches offline players, is an optional extra. Mail keeps working whether private messages are on or off. # How to turn it on In plugins/Chatalyst/players.yml : yaml Copy They are part of chat and ship on. title: Colors & nicknames
description: Nicknames that become the player's identity everywhere, with anti-impersonation, plus nick and chat colors, gradients and styles from a menu.
text: A nickname in Chatalyst is more than decoration. It becomes the name other players see in chat, the tab list, above the head, in the mailbox and in menus, and Chatalyst's own commands accept it as if it were the real name. Nicknames pass the same defenses as chat: invisible characters are removed, the rules and swear filter apply, and nobody can take another player's name. Players then color their nickname and their chat from two menus. # How to turn it on Nicknames and colors are always available. Access is controlled by permissions: /nick needs chatalyst.nick and colors need chatalyst.nick.color , both op by default. Grant them to the ranks that should have them. /chatcolor is open to everyone. title: Join, quit & death messages
description: Replace the plain vanilla join, quit and death lines with styled ones, greet players with a MOTD, and give high ranks a fancy entrance.
text: These are the lines everyone sees when a player joins, leaves or dies, plus the welcome message a player gets when they join. Chatalyst replaces the plain vanilla lines with styled ones in each player's language, and can give important ranks a little show when they arrive. Join, quit and death messages and the MOTD are on by default. Kick messages, fancy entrances and death effects are off. Everything is in plugins/Chatalyst/messages.yml . # Join and quit lines yaml Copy Quit works the same way. A few things to know: With Use_Player_Language: true (the default), the text comes from the language files, so each player reads it in their own language. Set it to false to use your Message exactly as written. Enabled: false hides the line completely, vanilla included. Vanished staff are never announced. Players can hide these lines for themselves with /toggle joinquit . # Different lines for different players Add Groups to give some players their own lines. The first group whose conditions match wins, and one of its messages is picked at random: yaml Copy A group can require a permission ( Require_Permission ), a list of worlds ( Require_Worlds ) and, for deaths, a killer ( Require_Killer_Contains ). # Fancy entrances A fancy entrance is a small show when a high-rank player joins: a sound everyone hears, a harmless lightning flash, a broadcast line and a title on screen. Turn it on in messages.yml : yaml Copy The shipped tiers are owner , admin and vip , matched by LuckPerms group o

title: Filter, anti-spam & anti-bot
description: Keep chat clean automatically. A swear filter that sees through tricks, anti-spam with escalating mutes, anti-bot join delay, hidden-character protection, a command blocker and cooldowns.
text: These tools protect your chat without staff having to watch it all day. The swear filter catches insults even when players disguise them. The anti-spam stops floods and repeated messages and mutes repeat offenders for longer each time. The anti-bot stops accounts that join and spam in the same second. And staff get quick controls for when things get out of hand: lock the chat, slow it down or clear it. Most of these are on by default and live in moderation.yml ; the swear filter has its own file, swear.yml . For custom patterns (advertising, links…) see the rules engine . # Swear filter The filter looks for whole words, so it does not flag normal words that happen to contain a bad one ("disputa", "class", "cultura"). And it sees through the usual tricks: Trick Example it still catches Repeated letters putooooo Separators p.u.t.o , p u t o , p-u-t-o Leet speak put0 , @ , 4 , 3 , 1 , $ Accents pútà Look-alike letters Cyrillic letters that look Latin Sound-alike swaps kabron , pvto CamelCase LaPutaDeTuMadre The word list covers Spanish (Latin America and Spain), English and Portuguese. title: Rules engine
description: Write your own chat rules with patterns, conditions and actions. Block advertising, clean up spam, warn, punish, alert staff or run commands, in chat, signs, books and more.
text: The rules engine lets you decide what happens when someone writes something specific. Each rule looks for a pattern and, when it matches, does whatever you choose: block the message, replace part of it, warn the player, add warning points, tell staff, run a command, open a book, and more. Rules check more than chat. By default they also check commands, signs, books, item names in anvils and nicknames, so a player cannot dodge the anti-advertising rule by writing a server IP on a sign. Chatalyst ships with ready-made rules: anti-IP, anti-domain, anti-Discord-invite, a character-repeat cleaner and anti-caps. Everything lives in rules.yml . # Turning it on It is on by default: yaml Copy Apply_To decides where rules run besides chat. Ignore_Commands lists commands that are never checked; keep your login and password commands here. # Anatomy of a rule This is the anti-IP rule from the real file: yaml Copy # Matching Key What it does Match The regular expression to look for. Case-insensitive unless Case_Sensitive: true Priority Higher runs first. Default 0 Contexts Where the rule applies: CHAT , COMMAND , SIGN , BOOK , ANVIL , NICK . Empty = everywhere Ignore_Permission Players with this permission skip the rule Ignore_Contains If the message contains any of these texts, the rule is skipped Strip_Accents true ignores accents while searching, so pütä matches puta . The rest of the message is not changed Stop_After true stops checking more rules after this one matches Begins / Expire

title: Mutes, bans & warnings
description: Silence players with a mute or a soft mute, let warning points punish repeat offenders automatically, and lock or slow down the chat.
text: These are the chat moderation tools. A mute stops a player from talking. A soft mute lets them keep typing, but nobody else sees their messages. Warning points add up every time a player breaks a chat rule, and punish them automatically when they reach a limit. Mutes, warning points and the chat controls work out of the box. Bans, kicks and freezes are part of the optional staff suite . # Mute a player text Copy Time is optional: 10m , 2h , 1d , 1w . Without a time the mute is permanent. Mutes survive restarts. Both commands need chatalyst.command.mute (operators have it). A muted player cannot chat. By default they also cannot send mail, write on signs or books, rename items on an anvil, or use a few chat commands. You choose all of that in moderation.yml : yaml Copy /helpop is left out on purpose: a muted player can still reach the staff. # Soft mute Add -s to mute a player silently: text Copy The player can keep typing and sees their own messages as normal, but nobody else receives them. It is useful for a suspected spammer or troll who would just make a new account after a normal mute. A soft mute only hides public chat; the Mute options above do not apply to it. # Warning points Warning points are on by default. Each rule with Points in rules.yml (and the swear filter) adds points when a player breaks it. When the total reaches a threshold, Chatalyst runs the commands you list. Points reset after a while without new infractions. yaml Copy {player} and {points} are replac

title: Staff suite
description: An optional, menu-driven moderation toolkit with bans, kicks, freezes, connection bans, vanish, staff mode and inventory checks.
text: The staff suite gives your team everything to handle a problem player from one menu: ban, kick, freeze, vanish, check inventories and read a player's history. Staff do not need to memorize commands; /staff opens a dashboard with buttons for each action. It ships off , so Chatalyst never fights a staff plugin you already use. Turn it on only if you want Chatalyst to be your moderation plugin. # Turn it on In moderation.yml : yaml Copy Then restart the server or run /cht reload . While it is off, none of its commands are registered. # What it includes Tool Commands Dashboard /staff opens the menu: player list, reports, frozen players and tools. Punishments /kick , /warn , /ban , /tempban , /unban . Reasons come from presets or are typed privately. Connection bans /banip , /unbanip : block the account and its connection, kick shared accounts and ban new alts. Freeze /freeze , /unfreeze : stop a player for a review. Leaving during the review gives a permanent ban. Vanish and staff mode /vanish : invisible, silent and unable to change the world while watching. Inspection /invsee , /echest , /seen , /check (history, possible alts, notes). Notes /note : private notes about a player, shared by the team. Teleport /tpto , /tphere . Every tool also has Spanish aliases. The full list with permissions is in Commands ; chatalyst.staff.* gives all of them. # Who owns /ban, /kick and /vanish With the suite on, Chatalyst takes the plain command names even if another plugin registered them fir

title: Reports & support
description: Let players report others to staff with /report, handle each report as a ticket, and answer "is an admin online?" with a private support chat.
headings: Reports on Discord and on the map
text: Reports let a player tell your staff about a problem with /report <player> <reason> . Each report becomes a numbered ticket that staff claim, answer and close, so nothing is lost and everyone knows who is handling what. The player can follow their ticket and reply to staff. Support requests catch questions like "any admin online?" in chat and turn them into a private conversation with the right staff member. # Turn reports on Reports ship off. In moderation.yml : yaml Copy Run /cht reload . title: Spy & logs
description: Let trusted staff watch private messages, commands, signs and more, and review what was said or done later from daily logs.
text: Spy mode lets trusted staff see what happens outside public chat: private messages, signs, books, anvil renames, chests opened and fights started. Logs keep a daily record of chat and these events, so staff can check what happened after a complaint, even when nobody was watching. The chat log is on by default. Spy is available to operators straight away. # Spy mode text Copy With no arguments it opens a menu with the main switch and each spy type, showing which types your rank can see. /spy toggle switches it on or off, and /spy <player> watches only that player. The watched player is never told. Permission Sees chatalyst.spy Everything below, and can use /spy . chatalyst.spy.pm Private messages only. chatalyst.spy.command Commands only. chatalyst.spy.sign Signs only. chatalyst.spy.book Books only. chatalyst.spy.anvil Anvil renames only. chatalyst.spy.container Chests, barrels and mechanisms used, with coordinates. chatalyst.spy.combat A line when a fight starts and when someone is killed. chatalyst.spy.channel Party channel messages. Give each staff rank only the types it needs. chatalyst.spy.autoenable turns spy on when they join. # What spy covers Each type can be turned off in players.yml under Spy . title: Anonymous mode
description: An incognito mode for streamers and staff - a believable fake name and skin, with rank, tags and party hidden everywhere.
text: Anonymous mode lets a player play without being recognized. It is made for streamers and for staff who want to watch the server as an ordinary player. With /anonymous , the player gets a believable fake name and skin, and their rank, tags and party disappear from chat, the tab list, nametags and hovers. Staff can always find out who is behind an alias with /realname <alias> . # Turn it on Anonymous mode ships off. In players.yml : yaml Copy Run /cht reload . An alias never matches anyone who has played on your server. # What gets hidden Rank, /tag and party, in every chat format, the tab list, nametags, hovers and clicks. Money and time played in the chat hover. The real name in messages from other plugins, such as death messages, titles and action bars. text: First impressions matter. When someone joins your server for the first time, Chatalyst can announce it to everyone ("Let's welcome Steve, new on the server!") and run console commands for them, such as giving a starter kit or a starting permission. This only fires on a player's very first join. Returning players are not affected. # How to turn it on The newcomer module is off by default. text: Mail lets players write to each other even when the other player is offline. The inbox is a menu: each mail shows the sender's head, nickname and a preview. text: Minecraft can only draw the name above a player's head in one solid color. The floating nametag replaces it with a floating text line that shows the full style: gradients letter by letter, bold, the rank prefix, ItemsAdder icons and the AFK tag. You can add a second line above it for a title such as "KING OF EVERYTHING", and animate it. title: Live translation
description: Opt-in live chat translation into each player's client language through a LibreTranslate-compatible service, with caching and a safe fallback.
text: Live translation lets players who speak different languages read each other. A player who turns it on reads other-language chat in their Minecraft client's language. The sender and players who share the sender's language see the original message. It only touches what players write in chat. It never translates the plugin's own messages, menus, commands, bot replies or moderation notices: those stay exactly as you wrote them. Translation is opt-in twice: you enable it for the server, and each player chooses to turn it on for themselves. # How to turn it on Get a translation backend that speaks the LibreTranslate API. Two easy options: Self-host LibreTranslate (free, no key) and set Provider_Url: "http://127.0.0.1:5000/translate" . Use a hosted LibreTranslate endpoint and paste its API key. In plugins/Chatalyst/integrations.yml , fill in Provider_Url , set Enabled: true and run /cht reload . You can also do it from /cht gui . "Chat translation" now appears in each player's /toggle menu. It starts off; players turn it on with the menu or /toggle translate . yaml Copy # Configuration Option Default What it does Enabled false Turns translation on. It stays off while Provider_Url is empty. Provider_Url "" Full URL of the /translate endpoint. Api_Key "" API key, if your provider needs one. title: Player tools
description: The everyday tools players get with Chatalyst. AFK, personal toggles, ignore, /me, chat colors, item sharing in chat, item renaming, colored signs and the player list.
text: Besides chat itself, Chatalyst gives players a set of small tools that make the server nicer to use: marking themselves as away, turning off what they do not want to see, ignoring someone, choosing a chat color, showing an item or their inventory in chat, and more. Most of them work for everyone out of the box; a few are meant as rank perks and need a permission. Bigger player features have their own pages: private messages , mail , nicknames & colors , books , market and marriage . # AFK Players are marked as away after a while without moving, chatting or using commands. Only the player is told, privately; nothing is broadcast. /afk toggles it by hand. yaml Copy Option Default What it does Timeout_Seconds 300 Idle time before a player is marked AFK Tab_Suffix " <#C0B3D9>[AFK]" What {afk_tag} shows in the tab list Notify true Tells the player when they go AFK and come back Ignore_Vanished true Vanished staff are never marked AFK automatically (manual /afk still works) The status is available as {afk_tag} in formats and as %chatalyst_afk% for PlaceholderAPI and TAB. # Personal toggles /toggle opens a menu where each player turns features on or off for themselves. title: Auto responses
description: A chat bot that answers common player questions automatically, in each player's language, and only offers what your server really has.
headings: How it fits with the rest of the chat
text: New players ask the same questions again and again: how do I make money, how do I claim land, where is my purchase. The auto-response bot answers them for you. When a message looks like a known question, the bot replies a moment later with the answer you wrote, in the player's own language. It understands how people really type. "komo gano din3ro!!!" and "how do i make money" reach the same answer. And its answers can adapt to your server: a reply about money only mentions /jobs if /jobs exists, and only mentions the market if your market is on. Chatalyst ships with 44 ready-made answers in English and Spanish (money, balance, private messages, mail, channels, reports, Discord, ranks, homes, warps, land claims, kits, voting, PvP, lag and more). Edit, delete or add your own in bot.yml . # Turning it on It is an optional extra and ships off. Set Enabled: true and run /cht reload . The global settings are at the top of the Auto_Responses section in bot.yml : yaml Copy Warning Remember to turn the bot on: Enabled: false is the default. Players and ops can all use it. Option Default What it does Enabled false Turns the whole bot on or off Bypass_Permission chatalyst.bypass.autoresponse Messages from players with this permission never trigger the bot. Nobody has it by default, ops included: give it to staff if you want them silenced Auto_Language true Each player gets the answer in their client language (English or Spanish) Language en Fixed language ( en or es ) used when Auto_Lan

title: Custom commands
description: Create your own simple commands like /discord or /website that show a message or run console commands, without any coding.
headings: Example: a vote command that gives a reward
text: Custom commands are small commands you create yourself, such as /discord , /website or /vote . Each one can show a few lines of text and run console commands. You write them in a config file; no coding is needed. They are ready to use: the default file already includes /discord and /web as examples. # Create a command Open plugins/Chatalyst/integrations.yml and find Command_Aliases . This is the shipped example: yaml Copy Change the links to yours, or copy a block to make a new command. The name of the block ( discord , web ) is the command. Save and run /cht reload : new, changed and removed commands apply straight away, tab completion included. # Options Option What it does Aliases Other names for the same command, for example [dc] makes /dc work too. Permission Permission needed to use it. Empty means everyone. Messages Lines shown to the player. MiniMessage colors and links work. Messages_es Optional Spanish lines, shown to players whose game is in Spanish. Commands Console commands to run when the player uses it. # Example: a vote command that gives a reward yaml Copy {player_name} is replaced with the player who used the command. See Placeholders for more. Warning Commands run from the console every time the command is used. A reward like the one above can be repeated as often as the player wants, so only give rewards that are safe to repeat, or give the command a Permission . Tip To change what the player sees when they type a command that does not exist, use Unknown_C

title: Books & rules
description: Server books that open as a real Minecraft book. Write your rules or a help guide once, open it with a command, and edit it in game without touching files.
headings: Showing the rules at the right moment
text: Books are the nicest way to show longer text: your server rules, a guide for new players, a list of commands. Chatalyst opens them as a real written book, with colors, clickable text and placeholders such as the player's name. Players open a book with /book <name> ; staff can write and edit books in game by writing in a normal book and saving it. Two books come ready to edit: rules and help . # Configuration Books live in books.yml : yaml Copy Key What it does Title The book's title (MiniMessage) Author The author shown on the book Permission Permission needed to open it. Empty = everyone Pages One entry per page. Use \n for a line break Pages use MiniMessage , so you can add colors, hover text and clickable commands. Placeholders work too: {player_name} , your custom variables and PlaceholderAPI values. Tip A book page is small. If text runs off the page, split it into two pages rather than shrinking it. # Writing books in game You do not have to edit YAML. Staff with chatalyst.book.admin can: Run /book new to get an empty book and quill. Write the pages as in any Minecraft book. Colors and formatting are kept. Hold it and run /book save <name> [permission] to save it. Use - as the permission to make it public. The title and author are taken from the book if you signed it. To change an existing book, /book edit <name> gives you an editable copy with its current pages; change it and save it again with the same name. /book delete <name> removes it. # Opening books Command Who

title: Balance top
description: A menu ranking of the richest players, calculated in the background from Vault so opening it is instant, with real skins and current nicknames.
text: /baltop opens a ranking of the richest players on your server. It is a menu, not a wall of chat lines: each player appears with their head, current nickname, balance and position, with medals for the podium. The ranking is calculated in the background and cached, so opening it is instant even with thousands of players who have ever joined. # How to turn it on Balance top needs Vault and an economy plugin (for example EssentialsX). It is on by default in plugins/Chatalyst/economy.yml : yaml Copy If no compatible economy is found, the module stays inactive. # Configuration Option Default What it does Enabled true Turns /baltop on. Size 45 How many players are ranked. Maximum 54. Update_Interval 300 Seconds between background recalculations. Opening /baltop also asks for a fresh calculation, so a recent change in someone's balance shows up as soon as it finishes, without waiting for the next cycle. Repeated requests close together share one calculation. The balance line and rank line of each entry come from the language files ( baltop.gui-balance and baltop.gui-rank ), so you can restyle them without touching the plugin. See Languages & messages . # Commands and permissions Command Permission (default) What it does /baltop ( /moneytop , /balancetop , /richest ) chatalyst.command.baltop (true) Opens the ranking. # Limits The ranking reads balances through Vault. title: Market & trading
description: A built-in market with escrow, auctions and barter, face-to-face trades where nothing moves until both accept, and announcements for external shop plugins.
text: Chatalyst covers trading between players in three ways: Market ( /market ): players list items for sale or auction. The item goes into escrow at once, the listing is announced in the trade channel with clickable buy and bid buttons, and sales are negotiated in a window where the buyer can offer money, items or both. Direct trade ( /trade ): two players open a shared window, add items and money, and nothing moves until both confirm. External shop announcements : if you use AuctionHouse, QuickShop or a similar plugin, Chatalyst announces their listings in the trade and auction channels. The market and direct trade both ship disabled . Money needs Vault and an economy plugin. # How to turn it on In plugins/Chatalyst/economy.yml , set Market.Enabled: true and/or Trade.Enabled: true , then run /cht reload . Enable the trade and auction channels too if you want the announcements to be visible (they are also turned on automatically when a supported market plugin is detected). # Configuration # Market yaml Copy Option Default What it does Enabled false Turns the built-in market on. title: Rentals
description: Let players rent ranks and perks such as /fly with in-game money for a limited time, granted through LuckPerms and refunded automatically if anything fails.
text: Rentals give players a way to earn perks by playing. Instead of a rank or /fly being something only money from your store can buy, players rent it for a day or a week with in-game money. Paying customers keep the convenience; players who grind get a path of their own. Every rental is granted through LuckPerms with an expiry. There are no permanent rentals: a rental that never expires would be a sale. # How to turn it on Rentals need Vault with an economy plugin, and LuckPerms for ranks and permissions. Write at least one offer under Rental_Offers in plugins/Chatalyst/rentals.yml (see below). Set Rentals.Enabled: true and run /cht reload . Grant chatalyst.command.rental to the groups that may rent. Warning chatalyst.command.rental is not declared with a default in plugin.yml , so only operators have it until you grant it. Give it to your default group with LuckPerms, for example /lp group default permission set chatalyst.command.rental true . yaml Copy # Configuration # General Option Default What it does Enabled false Turns the rental menu and command on. It ships off because there are no offers until you write them. Command alquilar The command name. Command_Aliases rent , alquiler Extra names. A name another plugin already owns is skipped. Flight_Permissions essentials.fly Nodes that give flight. When such a rental expires, flight is turned off on the spot, with a warning a minute before and a soft landing. The command is registered while the server runs, not in plugin.yml

title: Giveaways
description: A live draw the whole server watches, with a warm-up, a spinning roulette of player heads, immunity while it spins and prizes from items to ranks and money.
text: A giveaway in Chatalyst is a live event. Staff start a draw, everyone gets a countdown, and then a roulette of player heads opens for every eligible player at the same moment. The wheel spins, slows down with rising ticks, and stops on the winner, who gets a title, a broadcast, a firework and the prize. Staff never win by default, and nobody can be hurt while the wheel is on their screen. # How to turn it on Giveaways are an optional extra and ship off, with two example prizes. Set Enabled: true and run /cht reload . Settings live in plugins/Chatalyst/giveaway.yml : yaml Copy Staff open /sorteo , pick a category, then a prize, then start. Or they type /sorteo start <prize id> [seconds] [amount] . # Configuration # How a draw runs Warm-up. Everyone is told a draw is about to start, with a chat line, a title and a draining boss bar, and a countdown in the last seconds. Start. The roulette opens for every eligible player at once and immunity switches on. Spin. Heads scroll past and slow down; the tick sound rises in pitch. Winner. Chosen at the very last step, at random among the players still online. Then the prize is handed over and immunity fades a few seconds later. title: Marriage
description: Players propose, marry in private or with a public ceremony and wedding march, and share a chest, a teleport and a line in the chat hover.
text: Marriage lets two players make it official. One proposes, the other accepts, and from then on their partner shows in the chat hover like a marriage certificate. Couples get a shared chest, a teleport to each other and a notice when the other comes online. The couple decides how public it is: a plain proposal is private, and asking for a ceremony turns it into a server event with an invitation, vows and a wedding march played note by note. # How to turn it on Marriage ships disabled . In plugins/Chatalyst/players.yml , set Enabled: true and run /cht reload : yaml Copy While it is off, /marry and /divorce only answer that the feature is disabled. The commands need chatalyst.command.marry , which everyone has by default; remove it from groups if you want marriage to be a rank perk. # Configuration # General Option Default What it does Enabled false Turns marriage on. Request_Timeout 60 Seconds a proposal stays open (minimum 10). Announce true Announces public weddings to the server, in each player's language. A plain /marry is always silent. Announce_Divorce false Announces divorces. Tag certificate line The hover line. {partner} is the spouse, {since} how long they have been married. The shipped formats/chat.yml shows {married_tag} in the name hover. For a single player it resolves to nothing and the line disappears. # Ceremony How What happens /marry <player> Private wedding. No announcement, title, sound or particles. /marry <player> boda Public wedding: invitation, vows, wed

title: Scheduled events
description: Announce upcoming server events, list them with /events, remind everyone before they start and tell joining players, all managed from a menu.
text: Scheduled events tell your players what is coming: a boss fight on Saturday at 20:00, a build contest, a drop party. Players see the upcoming events with /events , get a "starting soon" reminder before each one, and are told about nearby events when they join. Staff create and edit events from a menu, so nobody has to type dates by hand. # How to turn it on Events are always available and the list starts empty. Staff with chatalyst.command.events.admin open /events admin and create the first event from the menu: name, day, hour, minute, description and reminder, all with clicks. Join_Notice_Hours 24 Joining players are told about events within this many hours. 0 = off. The menu writes them for you, but you can also edit them by hand: Field What it does Name The event name (also used for English clients). Name_es Optional Spanish name. Description Optional one-line description. When Date and time as epoch milliseconds. The menu sets it for you. Remind_Minutes Minutes before the event to send the reminder. 0 = no reminder. title: Proxy & Redis networks
description: Run Chatalyst across a Velocity or BungeeCord network. Cross-server chat, signed network packets, Redis sync, and a network admin center for staff.
text: On a network, Chatalyst lets your servers talk to each other. Global chat can reach every backend, staff can see the chat of any server without joining it, announcements can go to the whole network, and staff can teleport to players on other servers. Every packet between servers is signed, so a modified client cannot fake one. You use one universal jar: install the same Chatalyst-<version>.jar on every Paper/Purpur backend and, if you use the native mode, in the proxy's plugins folder too. Paper, Velocity and BungeeCord each load only their own part of it. All settings are in network.yml . # Choosing a transport yaml Copy Mode What you install Best for legacy Nothing on the proxy Simple networks. Uses BungeeCord's built-in forwarding; needs a player online on the sending server native The same jar in the proxy's plugins folder Recommended. Local channels (world, region, party, frequency) stay local unless you mark them. # Network security Every packet between servers is signed (HMAC-SHA256) and old packets are rejected, so nobody can forge announcements, support messages or staff actions from a modified client. yaml Copy Velocity with modern forwarding : nothing to do. title: Discord bot
description: A two-way Discord bot built into Chatalyst. Chat bridge, account linking, rank and ban sync, punishment roles, and staff tools from Discord, with no DiscordSRV.
text: Chatalyst includes its own Discord bot. It connects when your server starts and disconnects when it stops, so there is no DiscordSRV, no external process and no webhook to maintain. One bot does everything: it mirrors chat both ways, links Minecraft accounts to Discord, keeps ranks and bans in sync, and gives your staff a private channel to handle reports and moderation from Discord. Everything is off by default. You turn on only the parts you want, in the Discord section of integrations.yml . Note This bot is yours: you create it and it serves your community. Kagi is a different bot. It runs the support tickets and author-issued licenses on the Kazuo Community Discord , is not part of the plugin and never connects to your server. # Creating the bot Open the Discord Developer Portal , click New Application , give it a name and create it. Open Bot and press Reset Token . Copy the token: it works like a password. Never share it. Under Privileged Gateway Intents , enable MESSAGE CONTENT INTENT . Enable SERVER MEMBERS INTENT too if you will sync ranks from Discord to Minecraft. Open Installation , keep Guild Install , and add the bot scope. Give it View Channels , Send Messages and Read Message History . Add Manage Roles for rank sync or the linked role, and Ban Members for ban sync. Use the install link to add the bot to your Discord server. In Discord, open User Settings > Advanced and turn on Developer Mode . Right-click your server and your chat channel to copy their IDs. title: Store, ranks & Tebex
description: Sell ranks and one-time goods through Tebex with deliveries that are never lost. Rank catalog, in-game storefront, item claims and purchase celebrations.
headings: Nothing paid for is ever lost
text: Chatalyst connects your Tebex store to the game without a second queue or a separate plugin. It sells two kinds of things, and treats them differently on purpose: Ranks are a state . The player holds the rank, it may expire, and if it ever goes missing Chatalyst puts it back. Ranks are defined in integrations.yml and repaired continuously. Goods (items, commands, money) are an event . They are handed over exactly once and never repeated, even if the command arrives twice. Goods are defined in store.yml . In both cases a purchase is written to disk before anything is given, because Tebex considers a command done the moment it sends it and never resends it. Nothing depends on Tebex retrying. Players browse everything in one in-game storefront, /ranks , and collect their goods with /store . Note You need the official Tebex plugin installed. Chatalyst uses its command executor and never polls Tebex a second time, which would risk delivering the same purchase twice. # The rank catalog Every rank is declared once in Rank_Catalog at the top of integrations.yml . The key ( vip below) is a stable ID used by Tebex, Discord and the storefront. title: Languages & messages
description: Every player sees Chatalyst in their own Minecraft language. Edit any message, add new languages, and understand how English and Spanish texts work in the config.
text: Chatalyst speaks each player's language. A player whose Minecraft client is set to Spanish reads every message, menu and notice in Spanish, while the player next to them reads the same thing in English. You do not configure anything per player: the plugin reads the language the client reports. Every text the plugin shows lives in the lang/ folder, so you can reword any message without touching code. English ( en_US ) and Spanish ( es_ES ) ship complete, and you can add any other language by dropping in a new file. # How the language is chosen In config.yml : yaml Copy Option Default What it does Locale en_US The default language. Used for the console, for server-wide broadcasts and for any player whose client language has no file Auto_Detect_Language true true : each player sees their own client language when a matching file exists. false : everyone sees Locale When a player joins, Chatalyst looks for a file in this order: The exact client language, for example pt_BR.yml . The same language from any country, for example pt_PT.yml for a pt_BR client. The default Locale . The language follows the client live: if a player changes their Minecraft language, the next message already uses the new one. # Editing messages Open plugins/Chatalyst/lang/en_US.yml (or es_ES.yml ), change the text, and run /chatalyst reload . Messages use MiniMessage , so colors, gradients, hover text and click actions all work: yaml Copy Words in braces such as {player} or {id} are filled in by the plugin.

headings: Settings that matter on big servers
text: Chatalyst is built to stay off your server's main thread and to run only the features you turn on. Most servers never need to touch anything here. Saved in the background Player data is kept in memory and written to disk or the database in batches, outside the main thread.
